stemMd: A ferry operator plans to replace staffed ticket booths with kiosks. Because kiosk transactions take less time, it predicts shorter queues throughout the day. Which information most weakens this prediction?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The kiosks display the destination clearly.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Many passengers needing assistance will wait for a single attendant, creating a separate bottleneck during busy periods.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Kiosk transactions are faster when completed without assistance.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The ferry route has operated for decades.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Some tickets are already sold online.

explanationMd: Faster service for uncomplicated transactions need not reduce the system’s total queue when assistance capacity becomes the limiting stage.

distractorRationale.d: Route age does not determine queuing after the change.
distractorRationale.e: Existing online sales alone do not show whether queues lengthen.
distractorRationale.c: That repeats the premise while leaving the bottleneck unresolved.
distractorRationale.a: Clear display may help transactions rather than undermine the prediction.
